Acquisition Mandate Checklist for Buyers

A useful acquisition mandate describes the business you want, why you want it, what you can invest and how you will make decisions. It should make it possible to reject unsuitable opportunities quickly.

Start a private enquiry ↗

Strategic rationale

Write the operating or investment problem the acquisition solves. Identify required capabilities and the alternatives to buying. List objective evidence of strategic fit.

Target screening

Record sectors, locations, size, profitability, stake preference, critical certifications, customer concentration and exclusions. Distinguish absolute requirements from preferences.

Funding and transaction constraints

Define equity capital, debt assumptions, approval process, willingness to retain seller equity and post-closing operating responsibilities. Enterprise value and total cash outlay are not interchangeable.

Execution readiness

Appoint an internal deal owner, agree response timelines and identify external legal, tax and diligence advisers. Specify what can be disclosed to owners and how confidential information should be exchanged.

Common questions

Can the mandate evolve during the search?

Yes. Update it deliberately when evidence changes and communicate revisions to origination partners.

General information only; not legal, tax or investment advice. Transaction availability, suitability and execution depend on the circumstances.
